name: character-led
title: Character-led film
summary: A 15-to-120-second film led by the brand's own mark as a character: it comes alive, wants something, meets a turn and settles back into the lockup.
use_when: The brand has a mark or motif with personality, and the story is easier to feel through a character than to explain.

beats.name: meet
beats.job: The mark comes alive; its first move is the brand's signature motion.

beats.name: want
beats.job: What it's after, tied to what the brand does for people.

beats.name: turn
beats.job: The signature moment: how it gets past.

beats.name: resolution
beats.job: It settles back into the lockup, with the call to action.

rules: Emotion comes from motion and timing, not from extra words.

character.source: The brand pack's motif (the motif rig: N-part marks, ripples, pulses and waves), moved by the brand's motion law.
rules: The character is the brand's own mark or motif. It gets a face only if the brand's look already has one.
It moves by the brand's motion law: its named eases, its duration scale and its overshoot policy.
Its moves read as intent (anticipation, follow-through) and never as idle wobble.
Mark rigs stay symmetric, and no loop runs faster than a 16-frame period (the motion gate checks both).
If it speaks, its voice is designed or from the library, never a clone of anyone except the owner's own verified voice.

captions.note: Vertical and square cuts burn their captions in and use shorter lines (32 and 36).

budget.note: The explainer row: a character film is crafted like one, whatever its length.
